run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T04:39:29Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained at the proxy layer: the only sizeable error-status signal on frontend-proxy is its 'ingress' (Envoy server) span, with 20.29 error spans in the 70-minute window versus 24,771 non-error ingress spans (~0.08%), while every other operation of the proxy and of the frontend has zero error spans. The frontend-proxy access log shows the error responses are HTTP 503 with Envoy response flag UC and response-code detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for upstream cluster 'frontend' (upstream host 100.71.53.109:8080, the frontend Service ClusterIP), i.e. the frontend terminated the connection before starting a response; logged request durations of 140-705 ms show the requests were in flight, not idle pooled connections. The failing frontend pod shows no crash or restart (restartCount 0, no lastState, no previous container instance, no Evicted/OOM evidence) and its own spans carry no error status, so the failure does not originate from a frontend-visible application error or from a failing backend dependency. What remains unproven is why the frontend closes those connections: the strongest candidate is frontend CPU saturation (usage ~0.098-0.101 cores against a 100m limit with 25-30% of CFS periods throttled while ingress traffic ramped ~6x) together with a working set above its stated 200Mi memory limit; this is a time-coincident hypothesis, not a demonstrated cause. The alert's stated ratio 0.0111 could not be reproduced or verified: the RequestErrorRate rule is not present in the queried Prometheus and the observed ratio is an order of magnitude lower.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's 'ingress' spans are the dominant error source in the window: increase over 03:39:29-04:49:29Z is 20.29 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for (service_name=frontend-proxy, span_name=ingress), versus 0 for frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' and 0 for every frontend operation (GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/*, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect).
Summed by service over the same 70-minute window, error spans are: frontend-proxy 20.29, recommendation 4.06, ad 3.05, fraud-detection 3.05, and 0 for accounting, frontend and payment.
The measured frontend-proxy error ratio is small: 20.29 error ingress spans against 24,771 non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) ingress spans in the 70-minute window, i.e. about 0.00082 (0.08%).

Per-10-minute ingress series: errors are 0 from 04:10:29Z through 04:15:29Z, then 1.06-1.08 at 04:16:29-04:18:29Z, rise to 3.16-9.47 between 04:19:29Z and 04:39:29Z and remain 2.18-7.37 through 04:49:29Z, while ingress span volume grows from ~994 per 10 min (04:10:29Z) to ~6500 per 10 min (04:25:29Z onwards).

The cumulative frontend-proxy ingress counter surfaces first in Prometheus at 04:09:29Z with 424 error and 6151 total ingress spans (already-accrued values from process start at 03:58:32Z), rising to 444 error and 30,563 total spans at 04:45:29Z; there are no samples for this metric before 04:09:29Z inside the authorized window.

frontend-proxy access logs record HTTP 503 with response flag UC and response-code detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}', upstream cluster 'frontend' and upstream host 100.71.53.109:8080, 95 bytes sent (local reply) and request durations 140-705 ms; lines run from 04:15:22Z (GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM) and 04:18:04Z, 04:19:30Z, 04:19:58Z, 04:20:43Z, 04:20:57Z, 04:23:33Z, 04:23:34Z, 04:29:18Z, 04:31:21Z, 04:32:04Z, 04:34:10Z, 04:37:33Z, 04:37:50Z, 04:39:03Z, 04:40:55Z, 04:43:08Z.

100.71.53.109 is the ClusterIP of the otel-demo 'frontend' Service (port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend), so the terminated connections are those from frontend-proxy to the frontend Service, not to another backend.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 (IP 100.96.2.93, node i-0ec8b1fcc1cb45b42) is Running, created 03:58:31Z, container 'frontend' restartCount 0, empty lastState, and no previous container instance; its spec limits are cpu 100m / memory 200Mi. frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth limits are cpu 30m / memory 50Mi.

Frontend container CPU usage is 0.098-0.101 cores at 04:19:29Z, 04:29:29Z and 04:39:29Z (equal to its 100m limit), versus 0.018 at 04:09:29Z and 0.048 at 04:49:29Z; its CFS throttled-period ratio is 0.249-0.302 across every sampled point from 04:09:29Z to 04:49:29Z.

Frontend container memory working set is 242,548,736 bytes at 04:09:29Z and rises monotonically to 263,622,656 bytes at 04:49:29Z, above the pod's stated 200Mi (209,715,200 byte) memory limit, with no restart or OOM termination recorded.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts (only flagd shows two containers, both ready), including cart, checkout, currency, payment, product-catalog, recommendation, ad, shipping, image-provider, kafka, valkey-cart, postgresql and otel-collector.

The load-generator was rolled out by its Deployment at 04:30:19-04:30:20Z: ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd scaled 0->1 (pod load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb, IP 100.96.5.145, restartCount 0), old ReplicaSet load-generator-57ffcd644 scaled 1->0 and pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 deleted; the image stays ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-load-generator. The 503s already existed at 04:15:22Z (client 100.96.5.114) and continue at 04:31:21Z and later (client 100.96.5.145).

The ad/fraud-detection/recommendation error spans occur only on flagd streaming operations (ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 1.05-1.09 per 10 min, fraud-detection same, recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 1.13 already at 04:10:29Z and ~1.05-1.09 thereafter), while their ResolveBoolean/ResolveInt operations stay at 0 throughout.

The trace backend holds no spans newer than 04:12:47Z: the rows returned for the full 24-hour window are recorded 04:12:45.86-04:12:47.18Z, and the sampled 40 rows are frontend-proxy ingress/egress spans with status tag http.status_code=200, so the 04:15-04:43Z 503s have no trace coverage.

frontend-proxy itself is not failing its own work: its 'router frontend egress' (client) spans have 0 error spans over the window, it has 0 restarts, 4.4-6.1% CFS throttled-period ratio (cpu usage ~0.026 cores against a 30m limit, memory ~41MB against 50Mi), so the errors are responses the proxy generated when its upstream terminated connections, not a proxy crash.

Most likely mechanism behind the 503s: the frontend pod, pinned at its 100m CPU limit (0.098-0.101 cores) with 25-30% of CFS periods throttled while request volume to the proxy ramped from ~994 to ~6500 spans per 10 minutes, cannot complete a small fraction of in-flight requests and terminates their connections before sending response headers, which Envoy reports as upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}. This is a time-coincident correlation, not a proven cause; the same throttling ratio is already present at 04:09:29Z, and the deepest cause inside the frontend process was not observable.

Alternative mechanism: the frontend closes otherwise healthy HTTP/1.1 connections (Node.js/Next.js keep-alive or handler-level connection termination), which Envoy reports as UC{connection_termination}; the recorded 140-705 ms request durations mean the connections were in use when terminated, which is longer than a pure idle keep-alive race would explain, so this alone is a weak explanation.

A contributing factor may be frontend memory pressure: the container's working set (242-264 MB) exceeds its stated 200Mi limit for the whole observed period, which can stall or kill request handling; no OOMKilled termination or restart was observed, so memory pressure alone is not demonstrated as the cause.

Rejected: a frontend container crash, OOM kill or restart as the cause of the 503s — the frontend container has restartCount 0, an empty lastState, no previous container instance and no Evicted/OOM event, and it has been running continuously since 03:58:32Z.

Rejected: the load-generator rollout at 04:30:19Z as the cause — the first logged 503 predates it at 04:15:22Z from client 100.96.5.114 and identical 503 UC lines continue after it from the new client 100.96.5.145.

Rejected: a failing downstream dependency of the frontend as the cause — the frontend's client spans to its dependencies (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect) all show 0 error spans over 70 minutes, and every dependency pod (cart, checkout, currency, payment, product-catalog, ad, recommendation, shipping) is Running and ready with 0 restarts.

Rejected: the flagd EventStream error spans in ad, fraud-detection and recommendation as the cause of this frontend-proxy alert — they belong to other services' long-lived streaming spans, are chronic at ~1 per 10 minutes from the first available sample (04:10:29Z), and the frontend's own spans (including calls to ad and recommendation) carry no error status.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the rule's expression, window and denominator are unknown, and the alert's stated current value 0.0111 (1.11%) could not be reproduced; the observed frontend-proxy error ratio is about 0.08%.

Prometheus holds no samples for the frontend-proxy span metric before 04:09:29Z, so no pre-incident baseline exists for error rate, CPU throttling, CPU usage or memory; the 424 error spans already accrued at 04:09:29Z cannot be attributed to a time interval.
Jaeger trace data ends at 04:12:47Z, so the 503 requests logged between 04:15:22Z and 04:43:08Z have no trace coverage and no per-request upstream/parent detail.

The frontend container emitted no stdout/stderr lines in any window read (03:58:32-04:10:00Z and 04:20-04:49:33Z), so no application-level log evidence exists for why the frontend terminates connections; whether the frontend actually logs is unverified.

No evidence identifies what the frontend process does at the moment it terminates a connection (no kernel, conntrack, node-level or application-internal metrics were available for this investigation).

Change history is not integrated (not_integrated: change_history), so deployment/spec changes are visible only through current Kubernetes objects and the few events retained; why all otel-demo pods were created at 03:58:29-31Z (and flagd got a new ReplicaSet at 04:00:12Z) is not established.

frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration (upstream connection pool, idle timeout, retry policy for the 'frontend' cluster) is baked into the container image and not present in the cluster ConfigMaps read, so the proxy-side contribution cannot be checked.
next_steps: Review the RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression, evaluation window, denominator) because the reported 0.0111 does not match the ~0.08% measured error ratio on frontend-proxy ingress spans.

Compare the frontend Deployment's cpu limit (100m) and memory limit (200Mi) with observed saturation (0.098-0.101 cores, 25-30% throttled periods, working set 242-264 MB) and with load-generator request volume; consider raising the limit or lowering load-generator concurrency as a controlled test.

Inspect and, if appropriate, tune the frontend-proxy (Envoy) upstream settings for the 'frontend' cluster, e.g. enabling retries on reset/connection-termination 503s and aligning upstream idle timeouts with the frontend's keep-alive behaviour.

Enable or collect frontend application logs (the container produced none) and add connection-level instrumentation so the reason the frontend terminates in-flight connections can be observed directly.
Check node i-0ec8b1fcc1cb45b42 (hosting frontend, frontend-proxy and several other demo pods) for network/conntrack or resource contention evidence covering 04:15-04:43Z.
